prev_row.boundary_rationale: A restrictive particle opens direct second-person-singular address to God, unattested earlier in this speech: אַךְ שְׁ֭תַּיִם אַל תַּ֣עַשׂ עִמָּדִ֑י “Only don't do two things to me” web:Job.13.20, immediately specified as כַּ֭פְּךָ מֵעָלַ֣י הַרְחַ֑ק “withdraw your hand far from me” web:Job.13.21. This address shift - from the friends, or from soliloquy about God in the third person, to God as direct addressee - is the strongest interior seam in this speech. The petition turns accusatory, לָֽמָּה פָנֶ֥יךָ תַסְתִּ֑יר וְתַחְשְׁבֵ֖נִי לְאוֹיֵ֣ב לָֽךְ “Why do you hide your face, and consider me your enemy?” web:Job.13.24, and lands in legal complaint: וְתָ֘שֵׂ֤ם בַּסַּ֨ד רַגְלַ֗י וְתִשְׁמ֥וֹר כָּל אָרְחוֹתָ֑י “You also put my feet in the stocks, and mark all my paths.” web:Job.13.27 (single-witness paseq, not cited as evidence), closing the chapter on וְ֭הוּא כְּרָקָ֣ב יִבְלֶ֑ה כְּ֝בֶ֗גֶד “I am decaying like a rotten thing” web:Job.13.28. Job.13.28 itself already opens with an explicit third-person subject, וְ֭הוּא ('and he/it', continuing the moth-eaten-garment simile), rather than the second-person address to God that carries Job.13.20-Job.13.27; this row keeps Job.13.28 on its own side of the seam because the addressee (God, second person) still governs the verse's surrounding argument and no fresh discourse frame or vocative opens elsewhere, but the person shift is a genuine crux at the row's own far edge, disclosed rather than smoothed into an unbroken second-person run. The following row's fresh universal subject, 'man' in general rather than Job's own case, opens at Job.14.1.
prev_row.strongest_rejected_alternative: Extending this row through 14:6 to keep the entire divine-address arc in one span was considered and set aside, since a fresh universal subject opens chapter 14 as its own meditation rather than continuing the personal two-requests petition.
prev_row.literature_type_guess: Direct petition syntax with covenant-suit complaint

The dropped petition register, not the particle כִּ֤י itself (verse-initial כי is attested 82 times book-wide at skeleton tier -- 44 verses in the meteg-less form this verse's own opening carries and 38 verses in the meteg-bearing form כִּֽי -- and cannot alone carry a boundary) or any fresh third-person subject (Job.14.1 is already third-person), is what marks this turn. The analogy develops through מֵרֵ֣יחַ מַ֣יִם יַפְרִ֑חַ, “through the scent of water it will bud” web:Job.14.9, pivots to contrast at Job.14.10, וַיִּגְוַ֖ע אָדָ֣ם וְאַיּֽוֹ, “man gives up the spirit, and where is he?” web:Job.14.10, and closes on עַד בִּלְתִּ֣י שָׁ֭מַיִם לֹ֣א יָקִ֑יצוּ וְלֹֽא, “Until the heavens are no more, they will not awake” web:Job.14.12, before the wish-formula that opens the next row.

shipped_row.boundary_rationale: Job turns from describing the assault to his own response to it, fronting the object of his mourning ritual: שַׂ֣ק תָּ֭פַרְתִּי עֲלֵ֣י גִלְדִּ֑י, “I have sewed sackcloth on my skin, and have thrust my horn in the dust.” (web:Job.16.15), continued in his physical distress, “My face is red with weeping. Deep darkness is on my eyelids,” (web:Job.16.16), and closing on a protest of innocence, “although there is no violence in my hands, and my prayer is pure.” (web:Job.16.17). The preceding row's own opening also fronts a term before its verb (שָׁ֘לֵ֤ו הָיִ֨יתִי, 'I was at ease,' Job.16.12), so word order alone does not distinguish this row's edge; what changes at Job.16.15 is Job's grammatical role, from the described object of a third-person assault (Job.16.9-Job.16.14) to the grammatical subject of his own 1cs acts (שַׂ֣ק תָּ֭פַרְתִּי, 'I have sewed') — a participant-role shift, not the fronting by itself, marks the topic turn to Job's own mourning and innocence, a short unit that ends before the vocative apostrophe to the earth opens the next row.
shipped_row.strongest_rejected_alternative: Reading 16:15-17 as a continuation of the assault sequence would miss the fronted object that marks Job's own response as a new topic.
shipped_row.literature_type_guess: Weeping into dust with face-transformation imagery

prev_row.boundary_rationale: The row shifts from direct second-person address to third-person description of an assailant, “He has torn me in his wrath and persecuted me. He has gnashed on me with his teeth. My adversary sharpens his eyes on me.” (web:Job.16.9), through the crowd's mockery, “They have gaped on me with their mouth. They have struck me on the cheek reproachfully. They gather themselves together against me.” (web:Job.16.10), and the accusation against God directly, “God delivers me to the ungodly, and casts me into the hands of the wicked.” (web:Job.16.11), to a run of violent images closing on “He breaks me with breach on breach. He runs at me like a giant.” (web:Job.16.14). This third-person description of assault is a distinct register from both the retort to the friends and the singular address that precede it, and it gives way to Job's own self-description of mourning at 16:15.
prev_row.strongest_rejected_alternative: Merging this assault sequence with the mourning-ritual verses that follow would blend third-person description of what has been done to Job with his own direct response to it.
prev_row.literature_type_guess: Divine violence account personified assault metaphor

next_row.boundary_rationale: A vocative apostrophe opens the row, אֶ֭רֶץ אַל תְּכַסִּ֣י דָמִ֑י וְֽאַל יְהִ֥י מָ֝ק֗וֹם לְזַעֲקָתִֽי (oshb:Job.16.18) (“Earth, don't cover my blood. Let my cry have no place to rest.” (web:Job.16.18)), addressing the ground itself rather than the friends or the divine. The row continues on a 'behold'-headed clause, “Even now, behold, my witness is in heaven. He who vouches for me is on high.” (web:Job.16.19), through the friends' scorn, “My friends scoff at me. My eyes pour out tears to God,” (web:Job.16.20), the appeal itself, “that he would maintain the right of a man with God, of a son of man with his neighbor!” (web:Job.16.21), and closes on the approach of death: כִּֽי שְׁנ֣וֹת מִסְפָּ֣ר יֶאֱתָ֑יוּ וְאֹ֖רַח לֹא אָשׁ֣וּב אֶהֱלֹֽךְ (“For when a few years have come, I will go the way of no return.” web:Job.16.22), a ki-headed clause carrying its own finite verb pair. The next verse opens a new, asyndetic clause with a fresh subject and predicate sharing no verb with 16:22 — רוּחִ֣י חֻ֭בָּלָה יָמַ֥י נִזְעָ֗כוּ קְבָרִ֥ים לִֽי (“My spirit is consumed. My days are extinct and the grave is ready for me.” web:Job.17.1). The row crosses the chapter number on topic and address continuity alone: both verses share one mortality theme and no new addressee, formula, or particle intervenes between them, even though they are two grammatically separate clauses rather than one continuous sentence; the next shift comes at 17:2's oath-headed turn to the mockers.
next_row.strongest_rejected_alternative: Breaking this row at the chapter number between 16:22 and 17:1 would impose a metadata division at a point where topic and address run unbroken, even though the two verses are grammatically distinct clauses (16:22 ki-headed with its own verb pair; 17:1 asyndetic with a fresh subject and predicate) rather than one continuous sentence.
next_row.literature_type_guess: Blood-crying witness and advocate-seeking legal formulation

shipped_row.boundary_rationale: The row turns to Job's public humiliation, “But he has made me a byword of the people. They spit in my face.” (web:Job.17.6), and its physical toll, “My eye also is dim by reason of sorrow. All my members are as a shadow.” (web:Job.17.7), before pivoting to how the upright react to it, “Upright men will be astonished at this. The innocent will stir himself up against the godless.” (web:Job.17.8), and closing on a maxim of perseverance, “Yet the righteous will hold to his way. He who has clean hands will grow stronger and stronger.” (web:Job.17.9). This shame-to-maxim unit is a distinct topic from both the pledge-appeal before it and the direct address to the friends that reopens at 17:10.
shipped_row.strongest_rejected_alternative: Reading 17:6-9 as part of the pledge-appeal unit would miss the topic turn from a legal request to Job's public shame and the maxim that answers it.
shipped_row.literature_type_guess: Contempt-from-humans catalog with complete orphaning state

prev_row.boundary_rationale: An oath-type asseverative particle opens the row, אִם לֹ֣א הֲ֭תֻלִים עִמָּדִ֑י וּ֝בְהַמְּרוֹתָ֗ם תָּלַ֥ן עֵינִֽי (oshb:Job.17.2) (“Surely there are mockers with me. My eye dwells on their provocation.” (web:Job.17.2)), turning from the mortality clause just closed to a fresh complaint. The register shifts again to direct imperative petition, “Now give a pledge. Be collateral for me with yourself. Who is there who will strike hands with me?” (web:Job.17.3), before Job indicts the friends' understanding, “For you have hidden their heart from understanding, therefore you will not exalt them.” (web:Job.17.4), and closes on a curse-form judgment against betrayal, “He who denounces his friends for plunder, even the eyes of his children will fail.” (web:Job.17.5). The row ends there because 17:6 opens a new topic on Job's public shame.
prev_row.strongest_rejected_alternative: Attaching 17:2 to the death-wish unit before it would pass over the asseverative particle that opens a fresh complaint rather than continuing the mortality clause.
prev_row.literature_type_guess: Bargain petition for witness-advocate among the dead

next_row.boundary_rationale: The row opens on a direct address shift back to the friends, וְֽאוּלָ֗ם כֻּלָּ֣ם תָּ֭שֻׁבוּ וּבֹ֣אוּ נָ֑א וְלֹֽא אֶמְצָ֖א בָכֶ֣ם חָכָֽם (oshb:Job.17.10) (“But as for you all, come back. I will not find a wise man among you.” (web:Job.17.10)), a plural imperative that returns to the addressee of Job's opening retort after several rows of third-person and singular address. Job then turns to his own hopelessness, “My days are past. My plans are broken off, as are the thoughts of my heart.” (web:Job.17.11), through the death-imagery of “If I look for Sheol as my house, if I have spread my couch in the darkness,” (web:Job.17.13) and “if I have said to corruption, 'You are my father,' and to the worm, 'My mother,' and 'My sister,'” (web:Job.17.14), closing on “Shall it go down with me to the gates of Sheol, or descend together into the dust?” (web:Job.17.16). A paragraph mark follows this closing verse, oshb:Job.17.16 (samekh, single-witness), and Bildad's own vaya'an formula opens the very next verse, וַ֭יַּעַן בִּלְדַּ֥ד הַשֻּׁחִ֗י וַיֹּאמַֽר (oshb:Job.18.1), so the row's close coincides with the seam between Job's reply and Bildad's second speech: the formula-marked handoff to Bildad begins cleanly at Job.18.1.
next_row.strongest_rejected_alternative: Extending this row into 18:1 would carry Job's speech across the vaya'an formula that both the dialogue's formula spine and the paragraph mark at 17:16 treat as its close.

shipped_row.boundary_rationale: The speaker-change seam at Job.21.1|Job.22.1 opens this row: the previous row closes with Job answering (וַיַּ֥עַן אִיּ֗וֹב וַיֹּאמַֽר, oshb:Job.21.1), and this row opens with Eliphaz answering instead (וַ֭יַּעַן אֱלִיפַ֥ז הַֽתֵּמָנִ֗י וַיֹּאמַֽר, oshb:Job.22.1; “Then Eliphaz the Temanite answered,” web:Job.22.1). The formula's epithet is spelled defectively here (הַֽתֵּמָנִ֗י) against the fuller spelling Eliphaz's first two formula instances carry (הַֽתֵּימָנִ֗י, oshb:Job.4.1 and oshb:Job.15.1); swept independently, the defective spelling occurs at Job.22.1 alone (sweep: 1 book-wide) while the fuller spelling occurs 5 times book-wide, both in formula position and in narration (oshb:Job.2.11, oshb:Job.4.1, oshb:Job.15.1, oshb:Job.42.7, oshb:Job.42.9). Four verse-initial ha-interrogative tokens open this row in sequence — הַלְאֵ֥ל (Job.22.2), הַחֵ֣פֶץ (Job.22.3), הֲֽ֭מִיִּרְאָ֣תְךָ (Job.22.4), הֲלֹ֣א (Job.22.5) — the first three of which WEB's own punctuation further unpacks into four question-marked clauses, since Job.22.3's second colon (וְאִם בֶּ֝֗צַע כִּֽי תַתֵּ֥ם דְּרָכֶֽיךָ) is also rendered as a question though it opens on a mid-verse וְאִם rather than a fresh he-token; Job.22.5's הֲלֹ֣א (oshb:Job.22.5) sharpens the charge from piety to outright wickedness, setting up the itemized list that follows without yet stating it. Eliphaz's fifth and final ha-interrogative in this speech falls outside this row, at Job.22.12.
shipped_row.strongest_rejected_alternative: Ending the row at Job.22.4 and treating Job.22.5 as an opening line of the accusation catalogue was rejected, since Job.22.5 is still framed as an interrogative continuing the ha-prefixed question series of Job.22.2-Job.22.4, against the declarative register the catalogue itself uses from Job.22.6 on — a register contrast, not an asyndetic one: three of the catalogue's six verses (Job.22.6, Job.22.8, Job.22.11) open on overt connectives (כִּֽי, וְאִ֣ישׁ, אוֹ) rather than asyndetically, Job.22.6 itself a subordinating ki-clause.
shipped_row.literature_type_guess: Eliphaz's third-cycle response opening with piety-premise

prev_row.boundary_rationale: Direct address returns to close the chapter: הֵ֣ן יָ֭דַעְתִּי מַחְשְׁבֽוֹתֵיכֶ֑ם וּ֝מְזִמּ֗וֹת עָלַ֥י תַּחְמֹֽסוּ “Behold, I know your thoughts, the plans with which you would wrong me.” web:Job.21.27, answering the claim Job puts in the friends' own mouths — “Where is the house of the prince?” web:Job.21.28 — with an appeal to travelers' testimony (21:29) that the wicked man is spared for the day of calamity (21:30) and even honored at burial: וְ֭הוּא לִקְבָר֣וֹת יוּבָ֑ל “Yet he will be borne to the grave.” web:Job.21.32. The chapter closes on the same root with which it opened — וְ֭אֵיךְ תְּנַחֲמ֣וּנִי הָ֑בֶל “So how can you comfort me with nonsense” web:Job.21.34 answers “Let this be your consolation.” web:Job.21.2, תְּנַחֲמ֣וּנִי echoing תַּנְח֥וּמֹֽתֵיכֶֽם — turning the friends' own opening request back on them as a rebuke. A SAMEKH follows 21:34 (oshb:Job.21.34 (setumah, single-witness)), corroborating the close of Job's reply immediately before Eliphaz's third-speech formula opens at 22:1.
prev_row.strongest_rejected_alternative: Splitting off 21:32-34 as its own decision would separate the burial-honor image from the accusation it is answering.

next_row.boundary_rationale: The itemized accusation opens with an asyndetic ki-clause, כִּֽי (oshb:Job.22.6, “For you have taken pledges from your brother for nothing” web:Job.22.6), listing specific social wrongs charged directly against the addressee in the second person — withheld water and bread, web:Job.22.7 (תַּשְׁקֶ֑ה/תִּֽמְנַֽע, both 2ms) — interrupted at Job.22.8 by a third-person observation with no 2ms form anywhere in it, וְאִ֣ישׁ זְ֭רוֹעַ ל֣וֹ הָאָ֑רֶץ וּנְשׂ֥וּא פָ֝נִ֗ים יֵ֣שֶׁב בָּֽהּ (“But as for the mighty man, he had the earth. The honorable man, he lived in it.” web:Job.22.8), before the 2ms accusatory chain resumes at web:Job.22.9 (widows sent away empty, שִׁלַּ֣חְתָּ, 2ms; orphans' arms broken), before the unit closes with an explicit consequence particle, עַל כֵּ֭ן (oshb:Job.22.10, “Therefore snares are around you” web:Job.22.10), running through the floods-of-water image at Job.22.11. The whole span reads as one grounds-to-result movement: alleged sins, then their supposed effect on the accused.
next_row.strongest_rejected_alternative: Treating Job.22.6-Job.22.11 as a mere continuation of the preceding questions rather than its own row was set aside, because the consequence particle at Job.22.10 closes a self-contained list-then-result unit that the interrogative series before it does not share.
next_row.literature_type_guess: Indictment catalog Job's concrete social-injustice accusations

trigger_evidence.context: ster shift, disclosed as this row's best available ground, in fact falls one verse earlier, at Job.22.24|Job.22.25 insid
- at Writings-tier-3 weak strength, not as a driver - a break at the chapter's end, where Job's own vaya'an formula open

shipped_row.boundary_rationale: כִּי אָ֭ז (oshb:Job.22.26, “For then you will delight yourself in the Almighty” web:Job.22.26) continues, rather than reopens, the unbroken veqatal/result chain running from Job.22.23's protasis (אִם תָּשׁ֣וּב עַד שַׁ֭דַּי תִּבָּנֶ֑ה) through Job.22.24's imperative and Job.22.25's own waw-qatal consequent (וְהָיָ֣ה שַׁדַּ֣י בְּצָרֶ֑יךָ); no renewed protasis, address-shift, or formula marks Job.22.25|Job.22.26 itself. This row's material — delight in Shaddai, answered prayer, decreed authority, and rescue for the humble — closes the speech at Job.22.30 on the strength of that continuous chain; the appeal's own imperative-to-promise register shift, disclosed as this row's best available ground, in fact falls one verse earlier, at Job.22.24|Job.22.25 inside the preceding row (as at Job.22.21-Job.22.25), so it continues unbroken across this row's own opening rather than marking it. A petuchah follows Job.22.30 (oshb:Job.22.30 (petuchah, single-witness)), corroborating - at Writings-tier-3 weak strength, not as a driver - a break at the chapter's end, where Job's own vaya'an formula opens the next row.
shipped_row.strongest_rejected_alternative: Merging this row back into Job.22.21-Job.22.25 was declined not because Job.22.26 opens a distinct result movement — the veqatal chain from Job.22.23 runs unbroken through it — but because doing so would erase the petuchah's (single-witness) association with the speech's own genuine closing edge at Job.22.30, and because the register shift from imperative appeal (Job.22.21-Job.22.24) to sustained promise (from Job.22.25 on) still offers a defensible, if weaker, internal seam near this row's own opening.

prev_row.boundary_rationale: Address shifts from third-person description of the wicked to direct second-person imperative: הַסְכֶּן נָ֣א (oshb:Job.22.21, “Acquaint yourself with him now, and be at peace” web:Job.22.21), opening Eliphaz's closing appeal. The conditional particle אִם (oshb:Job.22.23) then sets the return-to-Shaddai protasis whose apodosis promises being built up, and the appeal continues through the treasure-exchange imagery of Job.22.24-Job.22.25 (laying gold in the dust in exchange for Shaddai himself as treasure).
prev_row.strongest_rejected_alternative: Keeping Job.22.21-Job.22.30 together as one ten-verse appeal was rejected in favor of a split at Job.22.25, though the chain's own consequent clause is already running by that point — וְהָיָ֣ה שַׁדַּ֣י בְּצָרֶ֑יךָ (Job.22.25) is itself a waw-qatal result clause, not a further protasis — and Job.22.26's own consequence particle simply continues that same result movement rather than opening a fresh one, so no clause-type boundary marks Job.22.25|Job.22.26 itself. The appeal's imperative-to-promise register shift (imperative at Job.22.21 and Job.22.23-Job.22.24, promise from Job.22.25 on) in fact falls one verse earlier, inside this row's own span, rather than at its Job.22.25|Job.22.26 close; the retained split is kept as a topical break within the continuous appeal-to-promise material, disclosed as weaker than a fresh clause-type opening.

next_row.boundary_rationale: Speaker changes again: where Job.22.1 opened Eliphaz's speech, this row opens with Job's own vaya'an, וַיַּ֥עַן אִיּ֗וֹב וַיֹּאמַֽר (oshb:Job.23.1, “Then Job answered,” web:Job.23.1). Job's complaint (Job.23.2) leads into the wish formula מִֽי יִתֵּ֣ן (oshb:Job.23.3, one of 9 verses book-wide carrying this formula, sweep: 9 book-wide), Job's desire to find God's seat and argue his case, set his cause in order, and be heard - a self-contained courtroom fantasy running through Job.23.7.
next_row.strongest_rejected_alternative: Closing the row at Job.23.5 and treating Job.23.6-Job.23.7 as a loosely attached coda was set aside, since those two verses complete the very courtroom scenario Job proposes in Job.23.4-Job.23.5 rather than opening a new topic.
next_row.literature_type_guess: Job's fifth-cycle speech opening with seeking-God orientation

shipped_row.boundary_rationale: This row opens with קַֽל ה֤וּא (oshb:Job.24.18, “They are foam on the surface of the waters. Their portion is cursed in the earth. They don’t turn into the way of the vineyards.” web:Job.24.18), describing the wicked as foam swept away and their portion cursed, running through Job.24.21's barren-widow imagery, then turns with וּמָשַׁ֣ךְ אַבִּירִ֣ים (oshb:Job.24.22, “Yet God preserves the mighty by his power” web:Job.24.22) to describe those same figures secured and watched over. No vaya'an, vayosef, address shift, or scene marker interrupts the MT between Job.24.17 and Job.24.24; the row is chunked as one continuous span for that reason, held rather than resolved. A register-based rival reading exists and is recorded, not adopted: some hear Job.24.18-Job.24.21's swift-perishing language as Job's own citation or ventriloquism of the friends' retribution doctrine (in tension with his complaint at Job.24.1 that Shaddai reserves no such days), rather than as Job's settled claim; the MT gives no formula or address-shift marker inside this span to decide between that rival and a straightforward reading, and no source-critical rearrangement is invoked to settle it.
shipped_row.strongest_rejected_alternative: Splitting this row at Job.24.21|Job.24.22 to separate the perishing description from the God-preserves turn was drafted and then dropped, because imposing a division there would assert a resolution to the passage's disputed register that no MT marker actually signals.
shipped_row.literature_type_guess: Wicked's perishing and preservation register tension

prev_row.boundary_rationale: A class-naming formula opens this row, הֵ֤מָּה הָיוּ֮ בְּֽמֹרְדֵ֫י א֥וֹר (oshb:Job.24.13, “These are of those who rebel against the light. They don’t know its ways, nor stay in its paths.” web:Job.24.13), introducing a distinct set of wrongdoers - the murderer, the adulterer, and the housebreaker - who operate by night and shun the light, closing with the terror of thick darkness at Job.24.17. The row itself is a coherent criminals-of-the-dark unit, but the material immediately after it (from Job.24.18) shifts register in a way this row does not itself extend into and does not attempt to resolve.
prev_row.strongest_rejected_alternative: Running this row through Job.24.24 as one long unit covering both the criminals-of-the-dark material and the perishing imagery after it was rejected, since Job.24.13's naming formula marks a class distinct from what follows, even where the material after it grows harder to place with confidence.
prev_row.literature_type_guess: Criminals operating under cover of night darkness

next_row.boundary_rationale: This closing part-seam row shifts to Job's own 1cs voice after the third-person wicked material that precedes it: וְאִם לֹ֣א אֵ֭פוֹ מִ֣י יַכְזִיבֵ֑נִי וְיָשֵׂ֥ם לְ֝אַ֗ל מִלָּתִֽי (oshb:Job.24.25, “If it isn’t so now, who will prove me a liar, and make my speech worth nothing?” web:Job.24.25), the interrogative מִ֣י carrying the challenge on the 1cs-suffixed יַכְזִיבֵ֑נִי and מִלָּתִֽי -- a legal-challenge formula that is a book-wide singleton (skeleton sweep: 1 book-wide for the two-word string) -- closing Job's whole reply before Bildad's own vaya'an opens the next part at Job.25.1 (“Then Bildad the Shuhite answered,” web:Job.25.1). A setumah follows Job.24.25 (oshb:Job.24.25 (setumah, single-witness)), corroborating -- at Writings-tier-3 weak strength -- a break exactly where the speech itself ends.
next_row.strongest_rejected_alternative: Folding this closing challenge back into the Job.24.18-Job.24.24 row was declined, since the return to Job's own direct address ('who will prove me a liar') is a distinct voice shift from the third-person description before it, and the setumah mark's (single-witness) association with a genuine edge would otherwise be lost.
next_row.literature_type_guess: Job's legal challenge daring proof of false speech
